construction_markdown:
Let
\[
p(T)=T^{15}+T+1,
\qquad F=\mathbb F_2[T]/(p),
\qquad q=|F|=2^{15},
\]
and let \(\operatorname{Tr}:F\to\mathbb F_2\) be the absolute trace.

View every \((x,y)\in F^2\) as a one-edge walk from the left to the right side of the complete bipartite graph \(K_{q,q}\). For
\[
P(X)=a_3X^3+a_5X^5+a_7X^7+a_9X^9,
\]
where \(a_3,a_5,a_7,a_9,u,v\in F\) and \(c\in\mathbb F_2\), define
\[
C_{P,u,v,c}(x,y)
 =c+\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(P(x)+ux+P(y)+vy\bigr).
\]
The code consists of all such vectors, ordered by the polynomial-basis binary indices of \(x\), then \(y\). Thus all \(q^2=2^{30}\) edges are used, with no padding, puncturing, shortening, or random choice.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Over \(F=\mathbb F_{2^{15}}\), take \(P=a_3X^3+a_5X^5+a_7X^7+a_9X^9\) and put \(c(x,y)=b+\operatorname{Tr}(P(x)+ux+P(y)+vy)\). The complete-bipartite edge correlation factors as \((-1)^bS(P+uX)S(P+vX)\). Weil and integrality give each factor at most 1448, hence a deterministic \([2^{30},91,\ge535822560]_2\) code.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Fix the two-endpoint, full-\(F\)-layer template with an \(r\)-dimensional shared nonlinear message, independent endpoint-linear layers, and distance certified only by factorization plus \(|S(Q)|\le(\deg Q-1)\sqrt q\). Two proper degree-\((2r-1)\) preimages cannot cover \(F^r\), so some message has both endpoint degrees at least \(2r+1\). The generic product certificate is then at least \((2r)^2q\); the budget \(64q\) forces \(r\le4\), hence \(k\le15(r+2)+1=91\).

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For an ordinary one-edge lift on a simple \(D\)-regular graph with \(vD=2^{30}\) and \(D<v\), powers-of-two arithmetic gives \(D\le2^{14}\) and \(D/v\le1/4\). Frobenius therefore gives \(\lambda^2\ge(v-D)/(D(v-1))>3/65536\), so \(\lambda>1/512\). Consequently the standard certificate \(B\le\varepsilon_0^2+\lambda(1-\varepsilon_0^2)\) cannot certify the required bias. Code-specific cancellation or a two-encoder bipartite analysis is necessary.

If P is nonzero, both endpoint polynomials have the same odd degree d in {3,5,7,9}; hence each character sum has magnitude at most (d-1)sqrt(q)<=8sqrt(q).
Character sums are integers, so each magnitude is at most floor(8sqrt(32768))=1448. Thus |W|<=1448^2=2,096,704.
Therefore every nonlinear word has weight at least (2^30-2,096,704)/2=535,822,560.
If P=0 and (u,v) is nonzero, a nontrivial linear-character factor vanishes, giving weight exactly 2^29.
If P=u=v=0, the only nonzero word is c=1, the all-one word. All nonzero cases are covered.

proof_markdown:
# Complete-bipartite trace-walk code

## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with parameters
\[
[2^{30},91,\ge535{,}822{,}560]_2.
\]
In particular, it exceeds the required distance by 224 and the verified dimension by 60.

## Explicit field

Put \(p(T)=T^{15}+T+1\). Repeated squaring modulo \(p\) gives
\[
T^{2^3}\equiv T^8,
\qquad T^{2^5}\equiv T^4+T^2,
\qquad T^{2^{15}}\equiv T.
\]
The two required coprimality checks have explicit remainder-one certificates:
\[
p=(T^7+1)(T^8+T)+1,
\]
and
\[
p=(T^{11}+T^9+T^8+T^7+T^4+T^2+T+1)(T^4+T^2+T)+1.
\]
Thus \(p\) is coprime to \(T^{2^3}+T\) and \(T^{2^5}+T\). Rabin's degree-15 criterion proves that \(p\) is irreducible. Hence
\[
F=\mathbb F_2[T]/(p)
\]
is a fixed field of size \(q=2^{15}\). Write \(\theta=T\bmod p\), use the polynomial basis \(1,\theta,\ldots,\theta^{14}\), and order field elements by their 15-bit coefficient integers.

The absolute trace is
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{14}z^{2^i}.
\]
Since \(\operatorname{Tr}(1)=1\), the character \(\psi(z)=(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(z)}\) is nontrivial.

## Construction, linearity, and length

Let
\[
P(X)=a_3X^3+a_5X^5+a_7X^7+a_9X^9,
\qquad a_3,a_5,a_7,a_9\in F.
\]
For \(u,v\in F\) and \(c\in\mathbb F_2\), define
\[
w_{P,u,v,c}(x,y)
=c+\operatorname{Tr}(P(x)+ux+P(y)+vy),
\qquad (x,y)\in F^2.
\]
Let \(C\) be the set of all these vectors.

Equivalently, take the complete bipartite graph with left and right vertex sets both equal to \(F\). Label a left endpoint \(x\) by \(\operatorname{Tr}(P(x)+ux)\), a right endpoint \(y\) by \(\operatorname{Tr}(P(y)+vy)\), and label the edge \((x,y)\) by the parity of its endpoint labels plus \(c\). Every one-edge walk is used.

Trace and evaluation are binary linear, so \(C\) is binary linear. There are
\[
|F|^2=2^{15}2^{15}=2^{30}
\]
coordinates, with no padding.

## Character-sum bound and factorization

For \(Q\in F[X]\), write
\[
S(Q)=\sum_{z\in F}\psi(Q(z)).
\]
If \(Q\) has positive odd degree \(d<q\), the additive-character Weil bound gives
\[
|S(Q)|\le(d-1)\sqrt q.
\]
For a codeword, direct separation of the two endpoint variables gives
\[
\sum_{x,y\in F}(-1)^{w_{P,u,v,c}(x,y)}
=(-1)^cS(P+uX)S(P+vX). \tag{1}
\]

Suppose \(P\ne0\), and let \(d\in\{3,5,7,9\}\) be its degree. Adding \(uX\) or \(vX\) does not change that top degree. Hence
\[
|S(P+uX)|,|S(P+vX)|\le8\sqrt{32768}.
\]
These character sums are integers, so
\[
|S(P+uX)|,|S(P+vX)|
\le\lfloor8\sqrt{32768}\rfloor=1448.
\]
Equation (1) therefore has magnitude at most
\[
1448^2=2{,}096{,}704=2^{21}-448. \tag{2}
\]

If \(P=0\) and \((u,v)\ne(0,0)\), at least one factor in (1) is the sum of a nontrivial linear character over \(F\), hence is zero. Such a word is exactly balanced. If \(P=u=v=0\), then \(c=0\) gives the zero word and \(c=1\) gives the all-one word.

## Dimension

The parameter space has binary dimension
\[
4\cdot15+15+15+1=91.
\]
The preceding case analysis proves injectivity. Indeed, if \(P\ne0\), (2) rules out a zero truth table, whose signed sum would be \(q^2\). If \(P=0\), a zero word has \(c=0\) by evaluating at \((0,0)\), and then nondegeneracy of the trace pairing forces \(u=v=0\). Thus \(\dim C=91\).

## Minimum distance

For a binary word of length \(q^2\) and signed sum \(W\), its weight is \((q^2-W)/2\). When \(P\ne0\), (2) gives
\[
\operatorname{wt}(w_{P,u,v,c})
\ge\frac{2^{30}-2{,}096{,}704}{2}
=535{,}822{,}560.
\]
The linear-only nonzero words have weight \(2^{29}\), and the constant-only nonzero word has weight \(2^{30}\). These cases exhaust every nonzero codeword, proving
\[
d_{\min}(C)\ge535{,}822{,}560
>535{,}822{,}336.
\]

## Scoped optimality of the template

Fix the same field and consider constructions with an \(r\)-dimensional shared \(F\)-message \(z\), two injective \(F\)-linear maps \(Q_1,Q_2\) into 2-reduced odd polynomials without constant or linear terms, two independent endpoint-linear coefficients, and one global binary constant. Suppose distance is certified only by factorization and the generic bound \(|S(Q)|\le(\deg Q-1)\sqrt q\).

For each endpoint, the nonlinear odd polynomials of degree at most \(2r-1\) form an \((r-1)\)-dimensional \(F\)-space. Their preimages under \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are therefore two proper subspaces of the \(r\)-dimensional message space. Two proper subspaces cannot cover a vector space, so some nonzero \(z\) lies in neither. Both endpoint degrees for this message are at least \(2r+1\). The numerical product bound supplied by the template is then at least
\[
(2r)^2q.
\]
The available correlation budget is \(2^{21}=64q\), forcing \(r\le4\). Consequently this proof template has
\[
k\le15r+15+15+1\le91.
\]
The submitted construction attains this scoped ceiling at \(r=4\). This is only a method obstruction: it does not cover restricted binary coefficient spaces, exact Walsh-spectrum cancellation, rational functions, or non-factorizing bivariate estimates.

proof_steps.statement: T^15+T+1 is irreducible over F_2, so the chosen quotient is F_{2^15}.

proof_steps.proof: Trace and polynomial evaluation are F_2-linear, and the coordinate set is exactly F^2.
proof_steps.statement: C is a deterministic binary linear code of length 2^30.

proof_steps.proof: Every nonzero shared polynomial retains an odd top degree d<=9 after adding either endpoint-linear term; the additive-character Weil bound and integrality give magnitude at most 1448.
proof_steps.statement: Each nonlinear endpoint character sum has magnitude at most 1448.

proof_steps.proof: The double character sum separates into the product of the two endpoint sums, up to the global constant sign.
proof_steps.statement: Every nonlinear complete-walk word has signed correlation at most 1448^2=2,096,704.

proof_steps.proof: The parameter space has dimension 91. The correlation bound excludes a nonlinear kernel; the trace pairing excludes a linear kernel.
proof_steps.statement: The encoder is injective and dim(C)=91.

proof_steps.proof: The weight/correlation identity gives 535,822,560 in the nonlinear case; linear-only words are balanced and the constant-only word is all-one.
proof_steps.statement: Every nonzero codeword has weight at least 535,822,560.
